newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close down 2.77 pct on labour unrest.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close down 2.77 pct on labour unrest.

text.p: Stocks lost ground across the board on Thursday as sentiment was badly affected by labour unrest following passage of a new labour law, brokers said.
The composite index provisionally closed at 659.01, down 2.77 percent or 18.75 points on the day.
An all-time record 920 stocks fell, compared with only 64 stocks that gained.
"The fall was due to the labour unrest," said an LG Securities broker. "Unions of many of the major companies, including Hyundai Motor, have declared strikes."

A controversial labour bill, allowing flexible work hours and lay-offs, was rammed through parliament on Thursday morning. In response, the outlawed Korea Confederation of Trade Unions called its 500,000 members out on strike, crippling key export industries.
"I see a series of massive strikes in the first quarter of 1997," said Namuh Rhee, head of research of Dongbang Peregrine Securities. "Workers have nothing to lose anymore."
Brokers said that buying by public pension funds just before the market's close pulled up the index from an intraday low of 655.24.
The funds focused on large-cap low-priced stocks, such as LG Chemical, traders said. LG ended unchanged at 8,570 won after falling to 8,200.
Daewoo Heavy Industries, which was hit by a union walkout, fell 190 won to 5,200 in heavy volume. Ssangyong Motors fell 800 won to 9,400, and Hyundai Motor lost 1,300 won to 20,000.
Hyundai Electronics' new shares closed their first day of trading down 1,800 won to their limit of 21,200.
